'''Nadia Magnenat Thalmann''' is a [[computer graphics]] scientist and roboticist and is the founder and head of MIRALab at the [[University of Geneva]]. She has chaired the Institute for Media Innovation at [[Nanyang Technological University]] (NTU), [[Singapore]] from 2009 to 2021.

==Biography==

Thalmann received an MS in psychology, an MS in biology and a Master in biochemistry at the University of Geneva. She obtained a PhD in Quantum Physics in 1977 from the same university. She started her career as an [[assistant professor]] at the University Laval in Canada, then became a professor at HEC, University of Montreal until 1988. In 1989, she moved to the University of Geneva where she founded the MIRALab laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About MIRALab |url=https://miralab.ch/about-miralab/ |access-date=2026-10-13 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Thalmann has authored and co-authored more than 600 papers in the area of Virtual Humans, social robots, VR, and 3D simulation of human articulations.{{Citation needed|date=December 2021}} She has participated in more than 45 European research projects.<ref>[http://www.miralab.ch/index.php/completed-projects/ European Research Projects]</ref> She has served the Computer Graphics community by creating the [[Computer Animation and Social Agents]] (CASA) in Geneva in 1988, as well as managing [[Computer Graphics International]] (CGI).{{Citation needed|date=December 2021}} She is the editor-in-chief of the journal ''The Visual Computer'' published by Springer, Germany<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Visual Computer|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/371/editors|access-date=2021-12-15|website=Springer|language=en}}</ref> and co editor-in-chief of the ''Computer Animation Journal'' published by Wiley.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Computer Animation & Virtual Worlds|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-sg/Computer+Animation+%26+Virtual+Worlds-p-9780JNRL33011|access-date=2021-12-15|website=Wiley.com|language=en-sg}}</ref>

==Research==
Thalmann has made numerous research contributions in the general area of computer graphics and is best known for her work on simulating realistic virtual humans. She also made early contributions in computer graphics during her PhD by simulating and visualizing 3D electronic densities of the [[Schrödinger equation]]'s approximate solutions (1977).<ref>N. Magnenat Thalmann, [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=zSucrdMAAAAJ&cstart=600&pagesize=100&citation_for_view=zSucrdMAAAAJ:RZBefGmQYygC A New Computer Program for Generating Three-Dimensional Plots of Electronic Densities and Related Contour Levels], Chimia, Swiss Chemical Society, vol. 31, no. 9, pp.361-362, 1977</ref><ref>N. Magnenat Thalmann and J. Weber, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0009261477850239 LCAO Xα calculation of the ionization energies of small molecules], Chemical Physics Letters, Elsevier, vol. 47, no. 3, 1977</ref>

Later on, she pioneered the modelling of realistic Virtual Humans, particularly producing the first simulation of a 3D version of [[Marilyn Monroe]]<ref>{{Cite news|last=Dabby|first=Victor|date=1987-06-16|title=And computer creates Marilyn|page=C6|work=The Ottawa Citizen}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=1987-05-21|title=Marilyn, Bogie star one more time|work=The Gazette|location=Montreal}}</ref><ref>Culture et Société, Montreal, May 21, 1987{{Full citation needed|date=December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Talbot|first=Paul-Henri|date=1987-05-23|title=Pour toute la famille|work=La Presse|location=Montreal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=1987-09-24|title=Elle met Marilyn sur ordinateur!|page=10|work=La Suisse|location=Geneva}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Sherman|first=David|date=1987-06-01|title=Film stars of the computer screen|work=Playback}}</ref> in the film [[Rendez-vous in Montreal]] (1987)<ref>[https://www.dropbox.com/s/ddau9elmjlo4h9v/28%20Os%20trukes%20da%20vangarda.pdf?dl=0 Os truques da vanguarda, Wednesday, November 25, 1987]</ref><ref>[https://www.dropbox.com/s/fugbw53tmstoisy/29%20Het%20Vrije%20Volk.pdf?dl=0 Het Vrije Volk, Saturday, June 27, 1987]</ref><ref>[https://www.dropbox.com/s/6ab4cnj30oi1mfh/31%20Eurographics.pdf?dl=0 Eurographics, Holland, November, 1987]</ref>

This film was shown in world premiere at the Place des Arts in Montreal to celebrate 100 years of engineering in Canada.<ref>[https://www.dropbox.com/s/w1ir38ml6bjvfrl/23%20Forum%20Premiere%20Mondiale.pdf?dl=0 World Premiere at the Place des Arts]</ref> She also showed her film at the Modern Art Museum in New York in 1988 along with Canadian computer artists.<ref>{{Cite news|last=van der Plas|first=Wim|date=1987|title=Animatie in Canada serieuze onderneming|language=nl|page=27|work=CADCAM}}</ref>

She made several original contributions in MRI segmentation methods correlated with clinical findings.<ref name="MRIsegmentation2010">J. Schmid, J. Kim and N. Magnenat Thalmann, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs11548-010-0474-z?LI=true Extreme Leg Motion Analysis of Professional Ballet Dancers via MRI Segmentation of Multiple Leg Postures], International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery (IF: 1.659), Springer, vol. 6, no.1, pp.45-57, May 2010</ref><ref>B. Gilles and N. Magnenat Thalmann, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1361841510000150 Musculoskeletal MRI Segmentation Using Multi-resolution Simplex Meshes with Medial Representations], Medical Image Analysis (IF: 3.681), Elsevier, vol.14, pp.291-302, June 2010</ref><ref>B. Gilles, F. Kolo-Christophe, N. Magnenat Thalmann, C. Becker, S. Duc, J. Menetrey and P. Hoffmeyer, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021929009001560 MRI-based Assessment of Hip Joint Translations], Journal of Biomechanics (IF: 2.496), vol. 42, no.9, pp.1201-1205, June 19, 2009</ref> She also modelled the simulation of Virtual Ballerinas where their hip cartilage deformations can be visualized while dancing.<ref>{{cite journal | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0363546510386002 | doi=10.1177/0363546510386002 | title=Assessment of Congruence and Impingement of the Hip Joint in Professional Ballet Dancers | year=2011 | last1=Charbonnier | first1=Caecilia | last2=Kolo | first2=Frank C. | last3=Duthon | first3=Victoria B. | last4=Magnenat-Thalmann | first4=Nadia | last5=Becker | first5=Christoph D. | last6=Hoffmeyer | first6=Pierre | last7=Menetrey | first7=Jacques | journal=The American Journal of Sports Medicine | volume=39 | issue=3 | pages=557–566 | pmid=21160017 | s2cid=46725738 | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="MRIsegmentation2010" /> She further demonstrates see-through knee articulations of real soccer players.<ref>A. Chincisan, K. Tecante, M. Becker, N. Magnenat Thalmann, C. Hurschler, H.F. Choi, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/26137896 A computational approach to calculate personalized pennation angle based on MRI: effect on motion analysis], Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery (IF: 1.66), DOI: 10.1007/s11548-015-1251-9, July 2015</ref> Since 2008, she has started at MIRALab, University of Geneva, a research with the humanoid robot EVA and demonstrated a first model of a realistic robot showing emotions and having a memory model.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00371-011-0630-7 | doi=10.1007/s00371-011-0630-7 | title=Building long-term relationships with virtual and robotic characters: The role of remembering | year=2012 | last1=Kasap | first1=Zerrin | last2=Magnenat-Thalmann | first2=Nadia | journal=The Visual Computer | volume=28 | pages=87–97 | s2cid=17756628 }}</ref> She has worked on the social autonomous robot [[Nadine Social Robot|Nadine]],<ref>[http://imi.ntu.edu.sg/IMIResearch/ResearchAreas/Pages/NadineSocialRobot.aspx Nadine]</ref><ref>[https://imi.ntu.edu.sg/NewsEvents/News/Press_Releases/Pages/2018.aspx Media coverage on Nadine]</ref> modeled in her image, that is able to speak, recognize people and gestures, express mood and emotions, and remember actions.<ref>J. Zhang J, N. Magnenat Thalmann and J. Zheng, [https://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=2915926.2915952 Combining Memory and Emotion With Dialog on Social Companion: A Review], Proceedings of the ACM 29th International Conference on Computer Animation and Social Agents (CASA 2016), pp. 1-9, Geneva, Switzerland, May 23–25, 2016</ref> Nadine has been shown at the [[ArtScience Museum]], in the exhibition HUMAN+: The Future of our Species, in Singapore, which has attracted more than 100 000 visitors.<ref>[https://www.marinabaysands.com/museum/exhibition-archive/human-plus/life-edges.html Nadine at the Singapore ArtScience Museum]</ref><ref>[https://imi.ntu.edu.sg/IMIResearch/ResearchAreas/Documents/Google/64_Channel_NewsAsia_190517_Singapore%E2%80%99s%20receptionist%20robot%20makes%20her%20public%20debut%20at%20ArtScience%20Museum%E2%80%99s%20futuristic%20show.pdf Media coverage on Nadine exhibition]</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

=== Honorary degrees ===
* In 2009, she was awarded a Doctor Honoris Causa in Natural sciences from [[Leibniz University Hannover]] (2009).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ehrendoktoren der Fakultäten|url=https://www.uni-hannover.de/de/universitaet/profil/ehrungen/von-der-leibniz-universitaet-verliehene-auszeichnungen/ehrendoktoren/|access-date=2021-12-15|website=Leibniz Universität Hannover|language=de}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=December 2021|reason=Source doesn't mention the year}}
* In 2010, Thalmann was awarded an honorary doctorate from the University of Ottawa.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.uottawa.ca/president/people/magnenat-thalmann-nadia |title=Honorary Doctorate of the University of Ottawa |access-date=August 17, 2017 |archive-date=August 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802124715/http://www.uottawa.ca/president/people/magnenat-thalmann-nadia |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Awards ===
*  In July 1987, Thalmann was named "Woman of the Year" by [[École des hautes études commerciales de Montréal]] for early original contribution in computer graphics in Montreal (1987).<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1987|title=Femme de l'année, catégorie scientifique|journal=HÉCHANGES - Journal de l'École des hautes études commerciales de Montréal|volume=3|issue=6}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1987|title=Un film québécois entièrement réalisé par ordinateur|journal=Journal des Ingénieurs|location=Québec}}</ref>
*In 2007, her film "High Fashion in Equations" has won the CGI 2007 Best International Scientific Video award and was shown at the SIGGRAPH Electronic Theatre.<ref>[http://www.scas.acad.bg/cs2007/index.php?lang=2&section=131&id=2 CGI 2007 Best International Scientific Video award]</ref><ref>[http://www.pauldebevec.com/CAF2007/ SIGGRAPH Electronic Theatre 2007]</ref> 
* In 2012, she has been a co-recipient of the Career Achievement Award by the Canadian Human Computer Communications Society in Toronto.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nadia Magnenat Thalmann|url=https://graphicsinterface.org/awards/chccs-scdhm-achievement/nadia-magnenat-thalmann/|access-date=2021-12-15|website=Graphics Interface|language=en-CA}}</ref>
* In 2012, she received the prestigious [[Humboldt Research Award]] in Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kaune|first=Juliane|date=2014-02-05|title=Die Vision vom durchsichtigen Menschen|url=https://www.haz.de/Hannover/Aus-der-Stadt/Uebersicht/Die-Vision-vom-durchsichtigen-Menschen|access-date=2021-12-15|website=HAZ – Hannoversche Allgemeine|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2012-06-05|title=DER TAG|language=de|pages=22|work=Die Tageszeitung: taz|url=https://taz.de/!587607/|access-date=2021-12-15|issn=0931-9085}}</ref>
*Thalmann selected as a Pioneer in Information Technology at the Heinz Nixdorf Computer Museum's Electronic Wall of Fame in Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|title=HNF - Pioniere der digitalen Welt|url=https://www.hnf.de/dauerausstellung/ausstellungsbereiche/wall-of-fame-pioniere-der-digitalen-welt/pioniere-der-digitalen-welt.html|access-date=2021-12-15|website=www.hnf.de|language=de}}</ref>
